note: Two lists, read by two different checks. Do not move an entry between them. `functions` is the source gate (scripts/check-anon-rpc-grants.mjs): functions in the public schema that OUR MIGRATIONS deliberately leave executable by anon or by PUBLIC. That list is exact, so an entry with no matching grant in the migrations fails as stale. `snapshot_objects` is the live catalog check (scripts/check-anon-acl-snapshot.mjs): objects a refreshed catalog snapshot shows reachable by anon, authenticated or PUBLIC on purpose. Most of those grants were never written by a migration, they are inherited from the schema default privileges, so they must NOT go in `functions`, where they would fail as stale entries by construction. Empty is the correct state for both. Adding a key to either is a security decision, not a formatting fix: it says that reach is intended. Paste the key the failing check prints rather than hand typing it, because the match is exact and case sensitive.
entry_shape: An entry is scoped to the grantees it names, so write it as "public.foo(uuid)": { "grantees": ["anon"], "reason": "one line, plain English" }. That excuses an anon grant on that object and nothing else: a PUBLIC or authenticated grant on the same object still fails, including one that shows up later and that nobody decided. `grantees` is required and must name PUBLIC, anon or authenticated, spelled exactly that way. A bare reason string, a missing `grantees`, an empty one, or any other role name is a hard parse error rather than a permissive default, because every lenient reading of a missing grantee is either an exemption nobody wrote or a line that quietly does nothing. Note that a NULL acl on a function is a PUBLIC grant, so it takes an entry naming PUBLIC, not anon.
